constraints.message: ManifestConsumptionReceipt.decisions[*].rule_id MUST be distinct. Each manifest rule gets exactly one decision; two decisions for the same rule_id make the receipt ambiguous about what was decided.
constraints.evaluation_note: Library-evaluated. The DSL form uses the registered unique_values builtin; validate() enforces the same rule through the registered ManifestConsumptionReceipt cross-field validator (validateManifestConsumptionReceipt), so fixtures under invalid-cross-field pass the structural tier and fail validate(). Join granularity is rule_id: a manifest may carry several entries with one rule_id (ORD-5 emits one per drift key), and one decision covers all of them.

constraints.expression: every decisions[*] satisfies decision == 'rejected' || decision == 'escalated' || judgement is non-empty; the schema requires judgement (minLength 1) for every decision, so the rule holds structurally and additionally rules out a rejected or escalated decision without a judgement.
constraints.message: Every ManifestConsumptionReceipt decision MUST carry a non-empty judgement, including rejected and escalated decisions. The judgement is the approver's answer to the contract row's judgement_requested question.
constraints.evaluation_note: Library-evaluable via the TypeBox structural tier: judgement is Type.String with minLength 1 and maxLength 1024 on every decision item. Restated here (SDD §3) so no reader concludes that rejected or escalated decisions may omit a judgement. Non-constraint MCR-N1: the library does not grade judgements; any non-empty string within bounds is accepted.

constraints.expression: consumer joins the receipt to the manifest identified by (schema_id, contract_version, manifest_emitted_at) and checks that every manifest rule_id has a decision, that no decision names a rule_id absent from the manifest, and that each decision's reason, when present, matches a manifest entry with that rule_id.
constraints.message: Every rule in the referenced UnverifiedObligationsManifest MUST have a decision in the receipt. The receipt does not embed the manifest, so completeness is checked by joining the two.
constraints.evaluation_note: Consumer-side join (ADR-010): the library does not hold the manifest when validating a receipt. joinReceiptToManifest(manifest, receipt) is the pure helper; its complete field is MCR-3 and its mc1_satisfied field adds the MC-1 fail-closed reading (no rejected or escalated decision). See docs/conformance/manifest-consumption-level-1.md.
